title: Lightning Events Detected from the International Space Station (ISS) 2017-2023
description: Lightning seen by the ISS Lightning Imaging Sensor from January 2017 to July 2023, drawn as yellow dots on a flat world map; we detected about 2.0 million new dots. Each drum hit is a cluster of new flashes: it is panned to where the storms are (west left, east right) and pitched by latitude, higher drums for northern storms. The bell line follows the average latitude of the storms, rising every northern summer and falling every southern summer, and the thunder rumble swells with the number of flashes.

legend.meaning: new lightning flashes; pan = longitude, drum pitch = latitude (higher = further north), loudness = flash brightness x count
average latitude of new flashes; higher = storm belt further north
constant background bed, not data-driven in this track

data_source.underlying: ISS LIS quality-controlled science data V1 (GHRC DAAC)
data_source.projection: equirectangular, lon -180..180, lat 90..-90 (Science On a Sphere)
data_source.calendar: movie time -> date by fitting the annual NH/SH flash cycle; see report.calendar
